summary.oneLiner:
Seshaasai delivered a strong Q4 (revenue +8.1% QoQ/+9.6% YoY, EBITDA margin 30.8% up 330bps YoY) on
better mix and operating leverage even as full-year FY26 revenue was flattish/down 1.5% YoY because the
core Payment Solutions card business (~50% of revenue) went through a renewal-cycle air-pocket (COVID-era
low base + bank renewal-policy tightening). The offsetting growth engines — Communication & Fulfilment
Solutions (+29% YoY) and IoT/RFID (+45-48% YoY, mgmt cites both figures) — plus a newly-commercialised SIM
card line (eSIM still pre-commercial) are the thesis for FY27, but management explicitly declined to give
formal FY27 guidance until after Q1, citing macro/geopolitical/FX uncertainty.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **No formal FY27 revenue/margin guidance given** — management (both Pragnyat Lalwani and CFO Pavan Kumar,
  asked by 3 separate analysts) explicitly deferred to "after Q1" citing geopolitical/macro/FX uncertainty.
- IoT segment: expects to **grow "upward of 47%"** YoY in FY27 (i.e., match/beat FY26's IoT growth, cited
  variously as 45% in segment note and 47-48% in Q&A — verbatim discrepancy, watch actual reported number).
- CFS: expects broad stability, "could be a marginal decline" but management "fine with that."
- Payment Solutions (base card business): expects renewal-cycle numbers to "bottom out" and trend upward
  from here, no quantified figure.
- Capex: **₹160-200cr planned for FY27** across Payment Solutions + IoT verticals + general modernization,
  partly funded from the ₹195cr unutilized IPO proceeds.
- eSIM: commercial revenue expected from **H2 FY27** once final GSMA compliance leg completes (targeted
  Jul-Aug 2026).
order book & pipeline:
- Won a multi-year tender from a leading PSU bank this quarter: ≈₹8.7cr revenue over the tender period.
- Domestic payment-scheme RFP and a global fintech RFP for metal-card variants — both still under
  evaluation, no revenue visibility yet (overseas RFP process ongoing ~4-5 months).
- 3 state-government transit-card projects underway (free-transport-for-citizens schemes); also working on
  metro-card rollouts as more metros come online.
- Customer additions FY26: 21 new in Payment Solutions (zero customer losses), 65 new in IoT, 8 new in CFS.
- Top-10 customers = 62.8% of FY26 revenue; >96.6% of revenue from existing customers (high repeat/renewal
  characteristic).
segment / subsidiary detail:
**Payment Solutions (~50% FY26 revenue, 47.5% of Q4 revenue):** Impacted in FY26 by (a) moderation in
issuance volumes from PSU/private banks, (b) lower renewal-card volumes due to a low COVID-era issuance base
~2 years back, (c) timing shifts in renewal cycles, (d) tighter regulatory/compliance environment for
banks/fintechs. Metal-card patent (filed Oct-2021, first Indian card manufacturer to do so; first global
payment-scheme approval for metal cards Mar-2023) was **granted Feb-2026**. Metal cards currently ~4% of
Payment Solutions revenue. India payment-card market share ~31.6% (per FY25 industry-analyst data, latest
published). Non-BFSI (system integrators for transit, forex/gift cards) ≈4% of the card business.

**Communication & Fulfilment Solutions / CFS (39% FY26 revenue, 39.8% of Q4 revenue, +29% YoY):** Platform-led
secure communication + fulfilment + traceability + logistics, built on proprietary RUBIC, eTaTrak, and IOMS
platforms plus pan-India execution infrastructure.

**IoT Solutions (11% FY26 revenue, 12.4% of Q4 revenue, +45% YoY per segment note / "47-48%" per Q&A):**
- RFID: capacity utilization ~70% average FY26, spiked to ~80-85% in Q4. Momentum building in a large Indian
  retailer's fashion-brand rollout (RFID + Bluetooth + sensor analytics); expanding beyond apparel into
  cosmetics/accessories; also renewables, healthcare, power-generation, GCC use cases. 65 new IoT customers
  added FY26.
- SIM cards: **began contributing materially to revenue in Q4FY26.** Installed capacity 7 million SIMs/month,
  current utilization ~30%. Already supplying a leading telecom player.
- eSIM: Bengaluru facility received **GSMA SAS-UP certification** in Q4 (SIM/eSIM manufacturing,
  personalization, PKI cert handling) — company says this makes it "one of the few global players" with this
  integrated capability. Not yet commercial; one more compliance process to complete by Jul-Aug 2026.
  Capacity 2-3 million eSIMs/month (varies by device form factor).
- Inlay manufacturing: in-house capability for 2.5 years, now 3 plants; working on RFID inlays for solar
  and cosmetics/healthcare; needs more scale before it is margin-meaningful.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Grocery and pharmaceuticals flagged as the two largest untapped RFID/traceability opportunities globally
  (already live in Europe/US); India likely to lag 12-18 months but small POCs already underway in pharma
  (India as a global pharma-outsourcing base).
- Tier-2 retailer RFID uptake building now that Tier-1 ROI is demonstrated.
- Textile export traceability: EU Digital Product Passport (EUDP) — company is a Walmart-approved RFID
  vendor; sees a "mixed bag" opportunity between RFID and conventional (QR/barcode) traceability depending on
  product criticality.
- International: working with local partners on a back-to-back basis in some geographies; export revenue
  only ~₹3cr in FY26 (immaterial); no plan to open an overseas personalization bureau this year; large
  overseas fintech player(s) have shortlisted the company in a global RFP (still under evaluation).
- Government single-card, multi-benefit platform — conceptual-stage pilot discussions with some state
  governments.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Patent-protected metal-card IP:** filed Oct-2021 (first Indian card manufacturer to do so), first global
  payment-scheme approval for metal cards Mar-2023, patent formally granted Feb-2026 — management stressed
  they have been commercially selling under this protection since filing, not waiting for grant.
- **GSMA SAS-UP certification** (Q4FY26, Bengaluru) for SIM/eSIM manufacturing + personalization — cited as a
  capability held by "few global players."
- **~31.6% share of India's payment-card market** (FY25 industry data) plus **Walmart-approved-vendor** status
  for RFID — evidence of scale/quality bar cleared with a marquee global retailer.
- **97-98% of revenue is recurring/annuity-like**, and >96.6% of FY26 revenue came from existing customers
  despite top-10 customer concentration of 62.8% — high switching cost / embedded-vendor position, not just
  customer concentration risk.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Gross margin improved ~150bps in Q4, a trend management says has been consistent for several quarters —
  driven by procurement consolidation, advanced inventory planning aligned to global trade cycles, and more
  efficient vendor payment terms; ~7-8% savings achieved at the material-consumed level (top 50% raw-material
  categories) for the full year.
- Adverse FX movement did hit Q4 input costs (large part of Q4 materials procured in late Q3/early Q4), but
  this was offset by operating leverage from higher QoQ sales.
- EBITDA margin +330bps YoY (Q4, to 30.8%) attributed to gross-margin gains + operating leverage + improved
  mix + procurement efficiencies.
- PAT margin (+316bps YoY, Q4, to 20.2%) additionally benefited from lower finance cost (post-IPO debt
  repayment) and interest income on parked IPO funds — flagged above as a non-repeating/quasi-one-off tailwind.
- Management explicitly would not commit to a margin trajectory for FY27, citing FX and input-cost
  uncertainty — will revisit after Q1.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- Navi Mumbai and Kundli facilities became operational in Q4FY26.
- **Nagpur and Bengaluru facilities still under construction — no commissioning date given; watch for
  slippage next quarter.**
- FY27 capex plan: ₹160-200cr across Payment Solutions + IoT + general modernization.
- Filed 6 new patent applications in FY26 (cumulative 19 filed, 5 granted to date).
capital allocation:
- Total IPO + pre-IPO proceeds ≈₹600cr; ₹405cr utilized by FY26-end, ₹195cr balance to be deployed in
  subsequent periods (per stated objects of the issue).
- Q4 IPO-fund utilization ≈₹60cr toward capex, general corporate purposes, and issue expenses.
- Board recommended a **dividend of ₹2.5/share**.
- Debt repaid post-IPO, reducing finance costs (contributing to margin expansion, see §7).
risks & watch-items:
- No formal FY27 guidance yet — first checkpoint is post-Q1 FY27 commentary; verify whether guidance is
  actually issued then and whether it validates the "IoT >47% growth" / "Payment bottoming out" narrative.
- Payment Solutions revenue has declined FY24→FY25→FY26; management says this should bottom out, but this is
  an assertion, not a confirmed inflection — track Q1/Q2 FY27 actuals closely.
- Nagpur/Bengaluru facility commissioning timeline undefined — slippage risk.
- eSIM commercialization contingent on completing final GSMA compliance step by Jul-Aug 2026 — watch for delay.
- FX/input-cost volatility called out by management itself as the key unresolved swing factor for FY27 margins.
- Working-capital days have risen over the last two years; management attributes this to inventory build
  (for supply-chain resilience) plus post-IPO cash inflating current assets, calling the underlying trend
  "more or less in line" — worth independently verifying via the cash-flow statement/receivable days.
- Two overseas RFPs (domestic payment-scheme metal-card RFP + global fintech RFP) remain unresolved with no
  revenue visibility.
management quality / tone:
Confident and fairly transparent: proactively clarified a recurring investor misconception around the metal-
card patent (protected since 2021 filing, not from the grant date), was forthright in attributing the
Payment Solutions decline to a COVID-base-effect + bank-renewal-policy factor rather than deflecting, and
consistently declined speculative FY27 guidance across at least four separate analyst prompts rather than
giving a soft number — a disciplined, if guidance-shy, posture. Addressed the post-IPO share-price/perception
question (Zaki Nasser) directly, reaffirming the pre-IPO business thesis is unchanged.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Management frames the company's ~25-year history as a series of ~5-7-year pivots (chequebooks → cards →
  RFID tags → SIM/eSIM), with a consistent capital-allocation "test" applied to each: recurring revenue,
  technology dependency, scalability, and "mandatory" nature of the product for the end customer.
- SIM manufacturing (physical card personalization) and eSIM (embedded-chip profile provisioning, no
  physical card) are distinct technical processes from each other and from RFID inlay/tag production —
  don't conflate the three IoT-adjacent revenue lines when modeling.
- Despite being called a "growth engine," metal cards are still only ~4% of Payment Solutions revenue —
  near-term P&L contribution is modest even as the segment scales.
- 97-98% of total revenue is recurring/annuity — the resilience thesis is largely independent of any single
  segment's cyclicality, which is the core defense against the FY26 Payment Solutions softness.
